reasons: Lake identity confirms case_name Kyles v. Whitley, court U.S. Supreme Court, date_decided 1995-04-19, and year 1995.
Lake citations confirm official 514 U.S. 419, parallels 115 S. Ct. 1555 and 131 L. Ed. 2d 490, and vendor cite 1995 U.S. LEXIS 2845.
Opinion text header also shows 514 U.S. 419 (1995), United States Supreme Court, decided April 19, 1995.
The opinion frames the case as arising under Brady and repeatedly discusses Brady materiality.
The opinion cites Giglio for prosecutor-office information-sharing duties and treats impeachment evidence as Brady material through Bagley.
The case refines Brady/Bagley materiality by emphasizing cumulative assessment and prosecutor responsibility for evidence known to police.
residual_risks: The target home-page taxonomy itself is not disclosed, so this verifies topical fit and role from the case materials, not a separate page definition.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: If the corpus distinguishes Brady from Giglio narrowly, label the home role as Brady/Bagley refinement with Giglio-relevant prosecutor-knowledge implications.

defect.evidence_quote: the prosecutor remains responsible for gauging that effect regardless of any failure by the police to bring favorable evidence to the prosecutor's attention
defect.problem: The stated holding is substantively supported as far as it goes, but the holding field announces two load-bearing points and then truncates after point one, omitting the prosecutor-duty point that the opinion itself treats as part of the holding.
defect.proposed_fix: Complete the holding field: materiality turns on the cumulative effect of all suppressed favorable evidence, and the prosecutor remains responsible for favorable evidence known to police or others acting on the government's behalf.

reasons: The cumulative-materiality portion is directly supported: the opinion says Bagley materiality is defined by suppressed evidence considered collectively, not item by item.
The omitted second point is also directly supported by the opinion's opening holding and later discussion of police-known evidence.
The phrase 'not item by item' should remain tied to final materiality assessment; the opinion separately notes that tendency and force may be evaluated item by item.
residual_risks: The inventory payload includes an ellipsis, so the full intended text may be outside the row; the built page frontmatter is nevertheless visibly truncated.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Add the prosecutor-duty point and, if space permits, a caveat that item-by-item evaluation is permissible before cumulative materiality is assessed.
